newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: French firm signs $20 million Cambodian map deal.
newsitem.headline: French firm signs $20 million Cambodian map deal.

text.p: IGN France International signed a $20.8 million deal with the Cambodian government that should help untangle land disputes in the country's capital, officials said on Friday.
Phnom Penh's confused history of land ownership has led to scores of lawsuits.

Under the two-year contract, IGN will study the city's land plots and provide maps, survey information and ownership details to the municipality of Phnom Penh beginning in January 1997, said Antoine de Chassy, IGN regional manager.
He said the project was supported by the Finnish government and the European Union.
Half of all court cases in Cambodia are land disputes, legal analysts say. Decades of civil war, followed by state ownership and hasty privatisation have left resentment among many citizens.
IGN, which is linked to France's national survey administration, provides land title service to nations in Africa, the Middle East and Southeast Asia, de Chassy said.
